task: Build a new freelance finance tracking phone app: an Expo (React Native) app for iOS and Android that uses the phone's camera to photograph receipts (with a photo-library fallback), plus a Python FastAPI backend (PostgreSQL in production; SQLite via DATABASE_URL for tests and previews). Features: JWT auth with the token kept in secure device storage; receipt capture and upload with amount, date, category and notes; mileage entry; a dashboard summary (income, expenses, mileage deduction, estimated tax); tax-ready PDF and CSV export shared through the phone's share sheet. The UI must be polished and professional, with a best‑practice sign‑up and sign‑in flow and clear navigation to every action. Use the current Expo SDK (look up versions with npm view; never guess). Includes unit and integration tests.

issues: The UI primary flow test fails because Playwright cannot locate and fill the "Email address" field on the Sign‑Up screen. The sign‑up form uses Unicode narrow‑no‑break spaces (U+202F) in the helper text (<Text style={styles.helper}>12 + characters, ...</Text>) which cause syntax errors during bundling and can prevent proper rendering of the component on the web. This results in the email input not being correctly associated with its label, so the locator times out. Fix the sign‑up screen by removing the problematic Unicode characters (use regular spaces) and ensure the TextInput has a proper `id`/`htmlFor` pairing and an explicit `aria-label` or `accessibilityLabel`. Also update the helper text to avoid non‑standard whitespace. After these changes the sign‑up page should render correctly and the primary flow test will be able to fill the email field and continue.

feedback": "The backend passes its unit tests, but the Expo UI has a critical failure: the Sign‑Up form cannot be interacted with by the automated UI test, likely due to the Unicode whitespace in the helper Text causing a bundling/parsing error and breaking the label‑input association. Clean up the SignUpScreen component (remove the U+202F characters, confirm the label’s htmlFor matches the input’s id, and add a stable aria‑label) and re‑run the UI flow test. Once the primary flow passes, all checks will be green and the solution can be approved.")

deployment_guide.app_type: mobile app (Expo / React Native), web service or API

ui.summary: Critical blocker: the Sign‑Up flow cannot locate the Email address input, breaking primary onboarding. Several required UI states (API error/offline on Dashboard, loading/error on Receipt/Mileage/Export) are missing, and accessibility details like visible focus indicators and SafeArea handling are incomplete. Minor styling inconsistencies and unsupported props are also present.

findings.issue: The Email address field is not discoverable by automation or screen readers – there is no visible label, nativeID, or proper accessibilityLabel, causing the primary sign‑up flow to fail at step 5.
findings.fix: Add a Text label "Email address" above the TextInput, assign a nativeID (e.g., "emailInput"), link the label via accessibilityLabelledBy, provide an accessibilityLabel on the TextInput, and ensure a testID is set for automated tests. Include placeholder and live validation as defined in DESIGN.md.

findings.issue: The Email address input suffers the same accessibility and labeling shortcomings as the Sign‑Up screen, preventing reliable sign‑in.
findings.fix: Mirror the fixes applied to Sign‑Up: add a visible label, nativeID, accessibilityLabel, and testID to the email TextInput, and ensure proper validation feedback.

findings.issue: Dashboard does not implement the API error and offline states required by the spec (banner messages, pull‑to‑refresh). Users see no feedback if data fails to load or when offline.
findings.fix: Create a Banner component that displays the exact messages "Failed to load data. Pull down to retry." and "You’re offline – data may be outdated.". Add a RefreshControl to the ScrollView to allow retry and update the UI accordingly.

findings.issue: Header is not wrapped in a SafeAreaView, so on phones with notches or status‑bars the title and settings icon can be obscured.
findings.fix: Wrap the header View with `<SafeAreaView edges={['top']}>` (or use `react-native-safe-area-context`'s `useSafeAreaInsets`) and adjust padding to respect the inset.

findings.issue: No visible focus indicator for keyboard/web navigation; spec requires a 2 px solid primary focus ring.
findings.fix: Add a `focused` style to the Pressable that applies `borderWidth: 2, borderColor: theme.colors.primary` and ensure it appears on web and when the component receives focus.

findings.issue: Overlay background color is hard‑coded (`rgba(0,0,0,0.3)`) instead of using a design token, violating the token‑first rule.
findings.fix: Add an `overlayBackground` token to `theme.colors` (e.g., `overlayBackground: 'rgba(0,0,0,0.3)'`) and reference it via `backgroundColor: theme.colors.overlayBackground`.

findings.issue: Prop `tabIndex={0}` is used on a React Native Pressable, which is not supported on native platforms and may generate warnings.
findings.fix: Remove `tabIndex` or guard it with `if (Platform.OS === 'web')` to apply only on web.

findings.issue: Form fields and buttons use browser-default styling with no custom design language, including placeholder text and border styles that feel unpolished.
findings.fix: Apply custom typography, rounded corners, and brand-aligned colors to form elements and buttons to create a cohesive, branded experience.

findings.issue: No visual hierarchy or spacing hierarchy: the 'Log in' button is not visually distinguished from the link below it, and there's no consistent padding or margin around elements.
findings.fix: Increase spacing between fields, add padding to the 'Log in' button, and use a larger, bolder font for the primary action to establish hierarchy.

findings.issue: The 'Don't have an account? Sign up' link is styled as plain text with underline, lacking visual emphasis or brand alignment.
findings.fix: Style the link with a distinct color, hover state, or subtle underline to make it more prominent and aligned with brand guidelines.

findings.issue: The layout is minimalistic with no intentional use of negative space or grouping, making the screen feel sparse and uncurated.
findings.fix: Add subtle visual grouping (e.g., a thin divider or padding) between the form and the link to improve visual structure.

findings.issue: visual quality 5/10 on 'sign in' (needs 8+): The sign-in screen is functional but lacks polish. It uses browser-default styling, has no visual hierarchy or brand identity, and the layout is minimalistic without intentional spacing or grouping. While it works, it doesn't feel like a premium product.
findings.fix: Address this screen's findings until it looks polished and professional.

findings.issue: Password field lacks a clear visual indicator for the password strength or validation status, relying only on text below the field.
findings.fix: Add a visual indicator (e.g., color-coded strength bar or icon) next to the password field to show validation status in real-time.

findings.issue: The 'Create account' button is centered but lacks subtle visual hierarchy to emphasize it as the primary action beyond color.
findings.fix: Add a slight drop shadow, rounded corners, or a subtle animation to make the button stand out more clearly as the primary action.

findings.issue: The 'Already have an account? Log in' link is centered but lacks visual weight or styling to indicate it's a secondary action.
findings.fix: Style the link with a lighter weight, smaller font, or a subtle underline to visually subordinate it to the primary action.

findings.issue: The password field's validation text is positioned directly below the field, which can be confusing for users unfamiliar with this pattern.
findings.fix: Move the validation text to the right side of the field or use a tooltip icon to avoid cluttering the space below the input.

findings.issue: visual quality 7/10 on 'sign up' (needs 8+): The sign-up screen is clean and functional with a clear primary action, but lacks visual polish and design sophistication expected in a premium product. Typography is readable but not refined, spacing is adequate but not exceptional, and there’s no desktop version shown for evaluation.
findings.fix: Address this screen's findings until it looks polished and professional.

went_well: All unit and integration tests passed, showing that the test suite is reliable.
The UI primary‑flow validator consistently detected the root problem (unable to locate the "Email address" field) across every round, giving a stable signal of failure.
The reviewer supplied concrete, actionable hints (e.g., remove invalid accessibilityRole, add proper labels) that were relevant to the failures.
The pipeline respected the coder turn‑limit and the repeat‑failure guard (no runaway loops).
Vision scores remained stable, indicating the visual evaluation component was not a bottleneck.

improvements.title: Add a UI accessibility static validator
improvements.evidence: Rounds 1‑6 all failed the UI primary‑flow validator on the same step (fill field "Email address"); reviewer repeatedly pointed to missing <label>, missing accessibilityLabel, invalid accessibilityRole, and Unicode whitespace (round 2‑5‑6). The coder hit its turn limit in rounds 1‑3, suggesting the issues were not caught early enough.
improvements.change: Extend validate.py (or add a new validator file) with a static checker that scans all JSX/TSX files for: • TextInput components with invalid accessibilityRole values (e.g., "textbox"); • Missing accessibilityLabel / placeholder / aria‑label that would expose a name to the web DOM; • nativeID misuse on web (nativeID not reflected as id attribute); • Presence of non‑ASCII whitespace (e.g., U+202F) in source strings. The validator must output file:line messages with a one‑sentence fix suggestion.
improvements.expected_effect: These UI‑accessibility errors are caught before the Playwright UI flow runs, giving the coder precise repair tasks, reducing turn‑limit hits, cutting token usage, and allowing the UI validator to pass earlier.

improvements.title: Make UI primary‑flow validator output actionable diagnostics
improvements.evidence: Raw validator output (rounds 1‑6) only reports a generic timeout: "locator.fill: Timeout 10000ms exceeded" without explaining why the field was invisible. Reviewers had to infer the cause, leading to overlapping advice each round.
improvements.change: Update ui_check.mjs to, on failure to locate a field, dump the ARIA/accessible name tree and report the specific missing attribute (e.g., "No element with accessible name 'Email address' found – check for accessibilityLabel, placeholder, or associated <label> with htmlFor linking to id"). Include a short recommendation (add accessibilityLabel or proper <label>).
improvements.expected_effect: Coder receives a clear root‑cause hint instead of a generic timeout, dramatically reduces guesswork, and speeds up convergence.

improvements.title: Tighten repeat‑failure guard for persistent UI validator failures
improvements.evidence: The same UI primary‑flow failure persisted for six consecutive rounds (rounds 1‑6). The pipeline allowed six attempts before stopping, consuming >5 hours and 143 coder calls.
improvements.change: Adjust the pipeline configuration so that if the exact same validator (e.g., "ui primary flow (expo‑app)") fails for 4 consecutive rounds, the run is halted and a redesign request is issued to the designer to amend ui_flow.json/DESIGN.md (e.g., add testIDs or explicit label mapping).
improvements.expected_effect: Prevents endless iteration on an unsolvable UI spec, forces an early design revision, and saves both compute time and token budget.

improvements.title: Consolidate reviewer feedback into a persistent prioritized TODO list
improvements.evidence: Reviewer issues changed each round (round 2: add <label>; round 3: nativeID↔id mismatch; round 5: add accessibilityLabel; round 6: remove Unicode narrow‑no‑break spaces). The coder received overlapping, sometimes contradictory hints, leading to repeated missed fixes.
improvements.change: Modify the reviewer prompt to output a structured "Pending Fixes" section that persists across rounds, marking items as resolved when a diff shows the change. Only new, unmet items are added each round. Present this list to the coder as the primary feedback message.
improvements.expected_effect: Provides the coder with a clear, incremental checklist, reduces duplicated suggestions, lowers token churn, and improves convergence speed.

improvements.title: Add a Unicode‑whitespace linter to static validation
improvements.evidence: Round 6 reviewer identified narrow‑no‑break spaces (U+202F) in helper text that caused bundling and label‑association errors, a problem that only surfaced after many iterations.
improvements.change: Extend the static validator suite (validate.py) with a rule that scans source files for non‑ASCII whitespace characters (e.g., U+202F, U+00A0) and reports file:line locations with a suggestion to replace them with normal spaces.
improvements.expected_effect: Catches invisible character bugs early, preventing bundling/parsing failures that break UI tests, thereby reducing wasted rounds.
